notes: Cr/Ni stainless-steel slag high-T gas-solid carbonation (tube furnace + fluidized bed) and low-replacement cement boards. Carbon uptake split to one row per temperature with its uptake (2026-11-10); values were only in notes.

1 Scientific Literature.Title: Feasibility study on carbon capture using stainless-steel slags
1 Scientific Literature.Study_Objective: Evaluate high-temperature dry and steam-assisted gas-solid carbonation of Cr/Ni stainless-steel slag in tube furnace and fluidized bed, and preliminary reuse in cement boards at 5-10%.
1 Scientific Literature.Abstract_or_Key_Finding: Carbon capture capacity rose from 500 to 750 °C, fell at 800 °C; temperature > carbonation time > particle size. 20% CO2 gave 65-80% of pure-CO2 capacity. 20% H2O/CO2 in fluidized bed gave highest U (22.60% at 750 °C vs 11.78% dry). 5% and 10% carbonated slag cement boards met local compressive threshold; 10% best thermal uniformity and low-frequency sound insulation.
1 Scientific Literature.Notes: Mainly carbon capture; construction use only preliminary.

2 Feedstock Chemistry.Source/Origin: Stainless-steel slag, steel plant in Tainan, Taiwan

3 Processing.Equipment_or_Process: Oven 100 °C; sieves 35/50/80/160 mesh; tube furnace; fluidized bed
